name: חֲנַנְיָהוּ
summary: The verb חָנַן “he has been gracious” with יָה, Yahweh. Borne by Hananiah son of Azzur, the prophet from Gibeon who broke Jeremiah's yoke and prophesied peace, of whom Jeremiah said, “Yahweh has not sent you”, and who died that year (Jer 28); by Daniel's companion, renamed Shadrach (Dan 1:6–7; 2:17), the Aramaic חֲנַנְיָה; and by many others: a captain of Uzziah (2Ch 26:11), a son of Heman the singer (1Ch 25:4, 23), a son of Zerubbabel (1Ch 3:19, 21), a Benjamite (1Ch 8:24), the father of Zedekiah the prince (Jer 36:12) and grandfather of Irijah (Jer 37:13), and in the return a son of Bebai (Ezr 10:28), a perfumer and a son of Shelemiah who built the wall (Neh 3:8, 30), the ruler of the citadel, “a faithful man who feared God above many” (Neh 7:2), one who sealed the covenant (Neh 10:24), a priest (Neh 12:12), and a trumpeter (Neh 12:41). The New Testament's Ἁνανίας is the same name (Act 5:1; 9:10; 23:2).

evidence.note: “חֲנַנְיָה son of Azzur the prophet, who was of Gibeon.”
“Yahweh has not sent you … this year you shall die”; and he died in the seventh month.
Among the sons of Judah, “Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah”; to Hananiah was given the name Shadrach.
The Aramaic spelling: “to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, his companions”.
“Hananiah the ruler of the citadel, for he was a faithful man and feared God above many.”
The verb of the name: “the children whom God has graciously given (חָנַן) your servant”.
Ἁνανίας, the disciple at Damascus: the same name in Greek.

note: Takes h.dz.ao (29 tokens, both spellings חֲנַנְיָהוּ and חֲנַנְיָה) and xh.ak.ab (BDB's Aramaic key for Dan 2:17, which the database fills with the same 29 tokens by spelling). TIPNR's Hananiah@Neh.10.23 is Neh 10:24 in the Hebrew numbering. TIPNR keeps fifteen people; whether some are one man (the Neh 3:30 son of Shelemiah and another) is TIPNR's judgement, kept as it stands. Scripture does not explain the name; the reading is the form, the verb חָנַן with the divine name.
